name: Twilight's Hammer
summary: Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, Twilight's Hammer works in secret to bring Azeroth to its end. Its creed calls for the Old Gods to awaken and all things to end.

sections.title: Origins in Shadow
sections.body: On Draenor, Twilight's Hammer began as an orc clan of the Old Horde. Two-headed ogre-mage Cho'gall led the clan and served as one of Gul'dan's chief lieutenants in the Shadow Council. Under Cho'gall, its members embraced a grim creed that looked toward the end of all things. They came to see the Horde as a force of destruction for that purpose.

sections.title: Arrival on Azeroth
sections.body:
Twilight's Hammer crossed the Dark Portal during the First War, and its apocalyptic zeal deepened on Azeroth. Its cultists heard the true whispers of the Old Gods, ancient horrors chained beneath the earth. Blackhand tolerated their erratic rituals because Cho'gall kept their bloodlust in check. He sent them with Kilrogg Deadeye's Bleeding Hollow clan in early assaults on Stormwind Keep.

During the Second War, the clan worked deep inside Grim Batol, overseeing critical refineries until Gul'dan's betrayal fractured the Horde. Orgrim Doomhammer ordered the traitorous clan slaughtered near the Tomb of Sargeras. A core of zealots survived.

sections.title: A Spreading Cancer
sections.body:
On Kalimdor's forgotten shores, Twilight's Hammer grew from a broken orc clan into a secret, multiracial conspiracy. It draws disillusioned members from both the Alliance and the Horde, recruiting any soul broken enough to welcome oblivion. In northern Kalimdor, Twilight Lord Kelris leads cultists entrenched in the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps. There they feed sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God.

Farther north in Darkshore, their excavators disturb the colossal fossilized remains at the Master's Glaive. In Silithus's southern deserts, robed fanatics tend abyssal windstones and listen for ancient horrors stirring beneath the sands.

faq.q: What is the Twilight's Hammer trying to achieve?
faq.answer: They seek to end all life and order on Azeroth. The cult calls oblivion a sacred blessing, not a path to conquest or wealth. It works to free the ancient Old Gods chained beneath the world.

faq.q: Are they an orc clan or a cult?
faq.answer: They began on Draenor as an orc clan led by Cho'gall. After fleeing the Second War, they left clan boundaries behind and became a secret, multiracial cult. They recruit humans, night elves, dwarves, and anyone willing to worship the Void.

Cho'gall founded and oversaw the cult. He is a cunning, two-headed ogre-mage and former apprentice of Gul'dan. Regional commanders lead local chapters, including Twilight Lord Kelris in Blackfathom Deeps.

faq.q: Why are they in Blackfathom Deeps?
aliases: what are they doing in ashenvale
faq.answer: Twilight Lord Kelris leads cultists occupying a sunken night elven temple along the Zoram Strand. They worship Aku'mai and feed sacrificial victims to the primordial three-headed hydra, a servant of an Old God.

faq.q: What are they doing at the Master's Glaive in Darkshore?
faq.answer: The Master's Glaive is a massive glaive embedded in a colossal creature's skull. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says an old, old lord of the earth fell there. Cultists gather to commune with lingering dark energies and seek signs of their masters' awakening.

faq.q: Why did Orgrim Doomhammer try to wipe them out?
faq.answer: During the Second War, Cho'gall and Gul'dan abandoned the Horde's march on Lordaeron to seek godhood at the Tomb of Sargeras. Their treachery cost the Horde its victory. Warchief Doomhammer sent loyal troops to slaughter the clans that had defected.

angles.text: As a priest, you draw on the same Void and shadow magic that Twilight's Hammer manipulates. The cult warns what can happen when communion with the whispers overwhelms mortal sanity.

As a warlock, you share the cult's past ties to Gul'dan's Shadow Council. Twilight's Hammer abandoned demonic fel mastery for the Old Gods' primordial madness, making its followers unpredictable rivals rather than allies.

As a member of the Horde, you inherit a shameful relic of the Old Horde's darkest days. Thrall's new Horde rejects the cult's madness and executes zealots who try to draw young orcs back into nihilism.
As a night elf, you see alien cultists defile sacred sites in northern Kalimdor, including Blackfathom Deeps and the Master's Glaive. Their presence assaults those lands in spirit and body.
